sections.overview: The Ocellated Turkey is a resident of the Yucatán Peninsula and adjacent northern Guatemala and Belize.
sections.identification: Its iridescent blue-green plumage and eye-like tail spots are characteristic.
sections.habitat: It mainly occupies mature lowland forest, including seasonally flooded forest edges and open areas used during breeding.
sections.diet: In one Campeche agroforestry study of males during breeding, crop contents were mostly seeds, especially maize and sorghum.
sections.behavior: It is resident rather than migratory, and uses clearings during the breeding season.
sections.reproduction: The female nests in a shallow scrape on the ground and lays about 8–15 eggs; incubation lasts roughly 28 days.
sections.ecology: Its foraging uses both forest and nearby agricultural habitat, making intact forest and the surrounding landscape relevant to its ecology.
sections.conservation: BirdLife classifies it as Near Threatened (2020), citing ongoing habitat loss and hunting pressure.
